issues.description: The template file template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not implement the expected Farm class defined in the problem statement and shown in the solution. Instead it declares a public class named AnimalFarm (mismatch with the required class name 'Farm'), contains a duplicate package declaration inside a method, malformed nested class content and mismatched braces. This creates a file/class name mismatch and renders the template uncompilable, which will confuse students and prevent them from implementing or testing the intended Farm class according to the UML and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Correct the template file to match the specification: ensure the file defines 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' once and declares 'public class Farm' (matching the file name). Remove duplicate/embedded package declarations and extraneous nested/malformed content so the class compiles. Provide the intended skeleton methods (constructor initializing animals list, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, and private singFarmSongVerse) as stubs so students can implement them following the UML.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named 'Farm' (with methods like addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong). The template repository's file Farm.java declares a class named 'AnimalFarm' instead of 'Farm'. This inconsistent class identifier (and the mismatch between file name and class name) breaks the direct mapping from the exercise description to the starter code, likely causing compilation errors and confusing students about where to implement the required methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template file to 'Farm' (public class Farm) so it matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the file name Farm.java contains public class Farm and provide the expected method stubs (addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong, get/set for animals) to align with the exercise description.
